content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text gives an UNDERDETERMINED verdict for D4 vs C2 based on how a phrase in Luke 2:48-49 is qualified by another phrase in the same verse, so it is deciding a single-verse ambiguity under the rule.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings is such a verse. It is not, if the judge names another verse or phrase that settles it.", "room": "\"another verse or phrase that settles it\": I weighed whether \"my Father's business\" is a settling phrase resolving the ambiguity, or whether it is merely the contrary reading within the same verse so that Luke 2:48-49 remains a verse admitting both readings.", "why": "The judge's UNDERDETERMINED verdict rests on the internal tension in Luke 2:48-49 between \"thy father\" and \"my Father's business,\" and the named phrase is not a separate settling verse or phrase but the competing reading itself."}
